what_fails: Permanent voter cards (PVCs) go uncollected and the register is never audited
evidence: 6,259,229 voter cards uncollected in 2023; 18.5% uncollected in Osun 2026 (INEC)

what_fails: Party crises and pre-election cases are settled by courts and INEC recognition
evidence: As of March 2026, one party held 31 of 36 governorships; two main opposition parties in court disputes (2026)

what_fails: Units open late and votes are bought
evidence: Officials at 27% of units by 7:30 a.m. in 2023 (Yiaga); N1,000 to N50,000 per vote in 2024 to 2026 state polls

what_fails: Violence and thugs keep voters away
evidence: 61% say violence could stop them voting, 78% in the North-East (Yiaga, Sep 2026)

what_fails: Polling unit result sheets reach IReV, INEC’s public results website, late, unreadable or not at all
evidence: 2023: 20% of presidential sheets online by noon the next day; 14.1% of units never usable online (CCIJ)

what_fails: Totals change while unit results are added up at ward, local government and state centres
evidence: Edo 2024: Yiaga found results altered at collation in three LGAs, with more than one party involved; Ekiti 2026: over 100 unit result sheets on IReV visibly altered (Dataphyte)

what_fails: Courts settle outcomes, and a failed upload alone does not void a result
evidence: 1,196 petitions after 2023; Supreme Court (Oct 2023): IReV is a viewing portal, not a collation centre, and a failure to upload does not by itself void an election
